note: Majority: not read. San Marino has no civil code; the age of majority sits in a statute (the 1986 family-law reform was looked for) that the Consiglio Grande e Generale's law archive, searched by title, didn't return to this client, and a web search found no text; null. Work: Legge 20 novembre 1990 n.137 (extending compulsory schooling to sixteen), article 8: employers may not make employment contracts with minors who haven't completed or been released from compulsory schooling, or in any case haven't turned sixteen; those who have turned fourteen may do seasonal work outside the school period (not held). The ILO's Child Labour Observatory profile (citing this law and Legge 9 dicembre 2022 n.164, the employment reform in force from 1 January 2023, whose text wasn't read) gives the general employment age as sixteen. Performers: no exception for performing is named, so barred under sixteen (my reading). Service: Legge 26 gennaio 1990 n.15 (Military Staff and Discipline; the Consiglio's English text), article 3: San Marino citizens are obliged to perform military service from sixteen to sixty; article 4: general mobilisation is ordered by the Great and General Council or, in extreme urgency, the Captains Regent, to defend the Republic or keep public order; article 9: service in the Uniformed Corps is voluntary. The ILO profile says recruitment is voluntary and the call of citizens aged sixteen to sixty applies only to a general mobilisation, never enacted. So none in peacetime, with the mobilisation duty noted here (my reading).

sources.title: Consiglio Grande e Generale: Legge 20 novembre 1990 n.137, Estensione dell'istruzione obbligatoria al 16 anno di età
sources.said: E' fatto divieto ai datori di lavoro di contrarre rapporti di lavoro con minori che non abbiano espletato o non siano stati prosciolti dall'obbligo scolastico, o comunque non abbiano compiuto il 16 anno di età.

sources.title: Consiglio Grande e Generale: Law no.15 of 26 January 1990, Regulating Military Staff and Discipline (English text)
sources.said: San Marino citizens shall be obliged to perform military service from the age of sixteen to the age of sixty. ... Military service in the Uniformed Corps shall be voluntary and shall be performed in the manner established by law and regulations.

sources.title: ILO Child Labour Observatory: Country profile San Marino
sources.said: The general employment age is 16 ... Law No. 15/1990 establishes that military recruitment is voluntary, although in exceptional circumstances of general mobilisation, citizens aged 16 to 60 may be called to defend the state.
